title: Three outlier scores — and why they disagree

explain.prompt: Compare the methods on RBOB daily log returns in 5–7 sentences: how many days does each flag, and why? Why does the classic z-score give only 1.3 to the hurricane day while the robust score gives about 10? Why does the IQR rule flag so many days? Which score could a desk have computed on the day itself, and why does that matter?
rubric: Classic z-score (|z| > 3) flags only the two fat-finger days: the ±2.3 log-point errors inflate the standard deviation so much that every genuine move looks small — masking. The hurricane day (+15 %) gets z ≈ 1.3.
Modified z-score uses the median and the MAD, which a few extremes cannot move: the hurricane day scores ≈ 9.6 and the error ≈ 150.
The IQR rule flags 16 days: commodity returns are fat-tailed, so 1.5 × IQR (calibrated on a normal distribution) treats ordinary large days as outliers.

Full-sample scores use future observations (the median, MAD and std of the whole sample): fine to describe history, not to flag a price in real time. The rolling score uses only the 60 previous days (shift(1)).
Detection is on returns, not price levels: on a trending level every new high would look like an outlier.
A flag is not a verdict: whether a flagged day is an error or an event is decided with other evidence (step 2.5).
